visuals.title: Where torsion happens
visuals.text: The spermatic cord twists above the testis, cutting off its own blood supply.

visual.label: 6-hour cut-off
visual.caption: Salvage rates fall sharply once torsion has lasted more than 6 hours.

glossary.Testis: The male gonad in the scrotum that makes sperm and testosterone; plural testes.
glossary.Scrotum: The skin pouch below the penis that holds the testes.
glossary.Bilateral: Affecting or done on both sides.
glossary.Acute: Coming on suddenly and over a short time.
glossary.Surgical emergency: A condition that needs an operation immediately to prevent death or permanent damage.
glossary.Adolescent: A young person going through puberty, roughly aged 10 to 19.
glossary.Reflex arc: The nerve pathway from a sensory nerve, through the spinal cord, to a motor nerve that produces an automatic response.
glossary.Afferent: Carrying signals towards the central nervous system, as sensory nerves do.
glossary.Efferent: Carrying signals away from the central nervous system to a muscle or gland.
glossary.Femoral branch: The branch of the genitofemoral nerve supplying skin of the upper inner thigh; the sensory limb of the cremasteric reflex.
glossary.Genital branch: The branch of the genitofemoral nerve that supplies the cremaster muscle; the motor limb of the cremasteric reflex.
glossary.Epididymis: The coiled tube on the back of the testis where sperm mature and are stored.
glossary.Infertility: Being unable to conceive after a year of regular unprotected sex.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test or best treatment available, against which others are judged.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from the history and examination alone, without waiting for tests.
glossary.Ultrasound: Imaging that uses high-frequency sound waves to show soft tissues in real time.
glossary.Theatre: The operating room where surgery takes place.
glossary.Oedema: Swelling caused by fluid leaking out of vessels into the tissues.
glossary.Venous outflow: Blood draining out of an organ through its veins.
glossary.Arterial inflow: Oxygenated blood entering an organ through its arteries.
glossary.Ischaemic time: How long a tissue has been without an adequate blood supply.
glossary.Rotation: Turning around an axis; in torsion, the testis spins on its cord.
glossary.Investment: In anatomy, how far a covering layer wraps around a structure.
